claims.claim: The power and interest grid is attributed to Aubrey Mendelow (1991); its quadrants are commonly labelled manage closely, keep satisfied, keep informed and monitor.
claims.source: Nielsen Norman Group 'Stakeholder Analysis', the Open University's OpenLearn and the Professional Academy, found by search on 13 November 2026; the 1991 paper itself was not checked.

concept_html:
A talent data platform touches many people: the HR director, the data protection officer, works councils, IT security, finance, HR business partners and the managers who read the reports. You cannot give everyone the same attention. A stakeholder map tells you where to spend it.

The power and interest grid. Score each stakeholder on two things. Power: how far they can help or block the work. Interest: how much the work affects them, and how much they care. The grid is often called Mendelow's matrix, after Aubrey Mendelow's 1991 work. Each quadrant has its own approach:

  • High power, high interest: manage closely. Involve them in decisions and meet them regularly. The HR director sits here.
  • High power, low interest: keep satisfied. Give short updates, and ask for little of their time. The chief information officer often sits here.
  • Low power, high interest: keep informed. Share progress and listen. HR business partners often sit here.
  • Low power, low interest: monitor. Check now and then that nothing has changed.

Add stance. Note whether each person supports the work, is neutral or opposes it. A powerful opponent needs a conversation early, not a surprise late.

Positions move. Announce an audit, and the data protection officer's interest jumps. Propose monitoring tools, and a works council gains power. Review the map at each phase of the work.

Turn the map into a plan. For each person, write what they care about, what you need from them, the channel and how often.

exercises.primer:
A `for` loop over `dict.items()` unpacks each key and value, and a tuple value unpacks too:

```python
scores = {"Ann": (4, 2), "Raj": (1, 5)}
for name, (maths, art) in scores.items():
    print(name, maths, art)
```

`isinstance(x, int)` checks for a whole number. `list.append(x)` adds an item to a list, and `sorted(a_list)` returns a sorted copy.

exercises.prompt:
Write `stakeholder_plan(stakeholders: dict[str, tuple[int, int]]) -> dict[str, list[str]]`. Each name maps to `(power, interest)`, each a whole number from 1 to 5. A score of 3 or more counts as high.

Return a dict with exactly four keys, `"manage closely"`, `"keep satisfied"`, `"keep informed"` and `"monitor"`, each holding the sorted names in that quadrant. Include every key, even when its list is empty. Raise `ValueError` for any score that is not an `int` from 1 to 5.
exercises.prompt_html:
Write stakeholder_plan(stakeholders: dict[str, tuple[int, int]]) -> dict[str, list[str]]. Each name maps to (power, interest), each a whole number from 1 to 5. A score of 3 or more counts as high.

Return a dict with exactly four keys, "manage closely", "keep satisfied", "keep informed" and "monitor", each holding the sorted names in that quadrant. Include every key, even when its list is empty. Raise ValueError for any score that is not an int from 1 to 5.
solution_lines: HIGH = 3
APPROACHES = ("manage closely", "keep satisfied", "keep informed", "monitor")
def stakeholder_plan(stakeholders: dict[str, tuple[int, int]]) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
"""Group stakeholders into the four power and interest approaches.
Args:
stakeholders: Name to (power, interest), each a whole number from 1 to 5.
Returns:
Each approach to the sorted names in it. All four approaches are present.
Raises:
ValueError: If a score is not an int from 1 to 5.
"""
plan: dict[str, list[str]] = {approach: [] for approach in APPROACHES}
for name, (power, interest) in stakeholders.items():
for score in (power, interest):
if not isinstance(score, int) or not 1 <= score <= 5:
raise ValueError(f"{name}: scores must be whole numbers from 1 to 5, got {score!r}")
if power >= HIGH:
approach = "manage closely" if interest >= HIGH else "keep satisfied"
else:
approach = "keep informed" if interest >= HIGH else "monitor"
plan[approach].append(name)
return {approach: sorted(names) for approach, names in plan.items()}

title: Map your stakeholders by power and interest
why_html: A people analytics team briefed the HR director weekly but sent the data protection officer one email at the start. Three weeks before launch, the DPO asked for a DPIA that nobody had started. The launch slipped two months. The DPO's power to stop the launch was always high. Their interest rose the moment personal data reached production.
